revenue_scope: Worldwide net product sales of Vyxeos as printed in Jazz's product sales table
geography: Worldwide (U.S. plus approved ex-U.S. markets per Jazz's 10-K)
moa: liposomal fixed-ratio daunorubicin and cytarabine (anthracycline plus antimetabolite)

approval_evidence.quote: NDA 209401 ... This new drug application provides for the use of VYXEOS (daunorubicin and cytarabine) liposome for injection for the treatment of adults with newly-diagnosed therapy-related acute myeloid leukemia (t-AML) or AML with myelodysplasia-related changes (AML-MRC). ... It is approved, effective on the date of this letter

launch_evidence.quote: Vyxeos net product sales in the third quarter of 2017 were $9.7 million. Vyxeos launched in the U.S. on August 11, 2017.

series_start_reason: First quarter with a Vyxeos line: the 2017Q2 release has no Vyxeos line (pre-launch); the Vyxeos launch in the U.S. on August 11, 2017 falls in Q3 2017.
notes: Jazz prints Vyxeos on its own line in every quarterly release from 2017Q3. Units: thousands USD through 2025Q4, millions USD in the 2026 releases (declared 'In millions'). Sum of printed quarters equals each full-year figure for 2018-2025 (checked).
search_log: Listed Jazz 8-K Item 2.02 filings from data.sec.gov (CIK 0001232524) back to 2018 and scanned every Ex. 99.1 financial press release for 'Vyxeos' rows (scan of 45 Item 2.02 filings 2018-2026 with January outlook releases carrying no table).
Each quarter taken from that quarter's own release (current three months, first figure); prior-year and year-to-date columns used only as cross-checks.

Cross-checks: each year's four quarters sum to the twelve-month figure printed in the Q4 release (2018 100,835; 2019 121,407; 2020 121,105; 2021 134,060; 2022 127,980; 2023 147,495; 2024 162,595; 2025 146,709).
FDA approval letter NDA 209401 fetched; approval paragraph quoted. The letter's signature date was not extracted.
Jazz 10-K FY2025 scope text checked: Vyxeos is commercialized in the U.S. and in approved markets in Europe and Australia and in Canada, which makes the printed line worldwide.
